_comment: Operator-configured encoder preference for tools/image-optimize (S0). Vendor-agnostic: the optimizer walks 'encoder_preference' top-to-bottom and uses the first adapter whose is_available() is true. Override the order without editing code via the IMAGE_OPTIMIZE_ENCODER_ORDER env var (comma-separated adapter ids, highest priority first), or point at a different config with --config <path>. No vendor is hard-coded in the engine; this list is data.

policy._comment: S1 format/sizing policy. Operator-configurable; CLI flags (--tier, --quality, --also-avif, --allowlist) and per-call opts override these. Tiers carry a max_width (never-upscale resize cap) and a max_bytes (post-encode hard-fail cap). A derivative over its tier's max_bytes FAILS the policy gate (CLI exit 2) unless allowlisted-with-reason.

_notes.encoder_preference: Default order. cwebp first (purpose-built WebP encoder, present locally at 1.6.0); sharp second (node module, no external binary). avifenc/pngquant/imagemagick are adapters that report unavailable on machines where the binary is absent — they never crash the run, they just get skipped. S0 only exercises the WebP-producing adapters (cwebp, sharp); the S1 policy engine uses sharp for resize+encode.
_notes.policy: S1: max_bytes defaults hero 250KB / content 100KB / thumb 50KB (KiB-based: 256000/102400/51200). max_width never upscales — a source narrower than the cap keeps its width. AVIF is off by default (--also-avif); it is always an additional derivative, never the sole asset.
